conventions.text: Labels are computed from the statutes by evals/gen/law.py and asserted against dates worked out by hand.
Posting date for the deemed-delivery fiction = the letter date, unless the letter states a separate posting date (spec.posted_on).

Deemed delivery: 3rd day after posting for items posted up to 2024-12-31, 4th day from 2025-01-01 (federal law and SGB X). A Land authority's letter counts its own Land's day (evals/law/laender.txt): Hessen the 3rd day; Hamburg the 4th from 2025-05-14 and Baden-Württemberg from 2025-02-07, the 3rd before; the other Länder with a text the 4th from 2025-01-01; in Baden-Württemberg, Bayern and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern a procedure begun before that Land's switch keeps the 3rd day when the letter states that start; a letter that states none is labelled as a procedure begun on or after the switch (the 4th day). AO moves a Sat/Sun/holiday fiction day to the next working day, VwVfG and SGB X do not. Remedy periods: one month (§§ 187 Abs. 1, 188 Abs. 2, 3 BGB), end moved off Sat/Sun/holidays; Bußgeld: two weeks after the Zustellung date on the envelope.

authority_region is set only when the letterhead names the Land; then expected_due uses that Land's holidays. When it is null, every dated item was verified to have the same date under all 16 Land calendars (so nationwide-only == legally correct).
No label depends on municipal-only holidays (Mariä Himmelfahrt in parts of BY, Fronleichnam in parts of SN/TH, Augsburg) — asserted.

Private-law payment/declaration deadlines are generated region-independent (place of performance is debatable); fixed dates in dunning and English letters fall on working days; Werktage periods never end on a Saturday — so no § 193 BGB edge case is labelled.

Municipal (Land VwVfG) letters come only from Länder whose delivery rule was checked against the Land's own published law (evals/law/laender.txt); never from Bremen, Rheinland-Pfalz, Saarland or Sachsen-Anhalt, whose text could not be read (evals/gen/law.py refuses them).
region_sensitive=true marks items whose date differs if the Land's holidays are ignored (due_if_region_ignored).
Remedy 'klage' (no Vorverfahren): the label is the end of the one-month Klage period (§ 74 Abs. 1 S. 2 VwGO), counted like the other remedy periods.
optional_items are dates a letter offers that the reader need not act on (e.g. special-cancellation windows, payments after Rechtskraft, scam demands); no label requires them.
expected_due 'ambiguous' (with candidates) marks a slot the letter leaves open between two or more dates; null marks one the letter gives no date for.
Photo entries are phone-photo renderings of page 1 of a one-page PDF entry (source_id) and share its truth.
today = the day the person reads the letter (posting/letter date + 2..6 days); it is not a receipt date.

Template wording: the test variants (C, D) and the adversarial letters repeat no deadline-bearing sentence of the dev variants (A, B); only short statutory phrases (e.g. 'vierten Tag nach Aufgabe zur Post') recur.

Holdout split: variants E, F and the holdout adversarial letters were written from scratch (new senders, recipients, wording, layout, dates and amounts) before the split's first run; they repeat no deadline-bearing sentence of the dev or test letters.

Holdout2 split: variants G, H and the holdout2 adversarial letters were written from scratch (new senders, recipients, wording, layout, dates, amounts and regions) after the release's last code change; they repeat no deadline-bearing sentence of the dev, test or holdout letters.

Holdout3 split: variants I, J and the holdout3 adversarial letters were written from scratch (new senders, recipients, wording, layout, dates, amounts and regions) after the code freeze; they repeat no deadline-bearing sentence of the dev, test, holdout or holdout2 letters.
references list identifiers only; info-block lines holding a dash, a date or a billing month are printed but not labelled.

amounts = the sums the reader must pay, will receive, or that the decision sets (old/new price for price changes, fees to bring to an appointment); line items, sums insured and merely threatened penalties are not listed.
remedy_type follows the letter's own Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung; kind_also_accepted names a second document kind that fits the letter equally well.

Consumer contracts under § 309 Nr. 9 BGB / § 56 TKG are generated so that the written minimum term also fits into 24 months from conclusion — the open question whether the cap counts from conclusion or from the start of service never matters.
A notice deadline (cancel-by) stays on a Saturday, Sunday or holiday: § 193 BGB does not apply to notice periods (BGH III ZR 172/04).

A letter that gives two different dates for the same obligation (two payment dates, or two calendar dates of the same decision from which its remedy period is counted): the label is the earlier date, the later one is listed among the candidates, and the item is marked for low assurance. Reading the letter against its drafter (§ 305c Abs. 2 BGB) or by the date printed in its header or payment box gives the later date.

24 and 31 December are working days: neither is a public holiday under federal law or any Land's holiday act, so a period that ends on either day stays there (§ 193 BGB, § 108 Abs. 3 AO, § 26 Abs. 3 SGB X, § 222 Abs. 2 ZPO).

A written declaration of a private sender that the letter says was handed to the addressee in person, or put into the addressee's letterbox by a messenger on a stated weekday in the morning, reaches the addressee on that day (§ 130 Abs. 1 S. 1 BGB); a period that runs from its receipt is counted from that day (§ 187 Abs. 1 BGB).

A court order served under the ZPO counts as served on the day the service note printed on it states (§ 180 S. 3, § 177 ZPO). Its two-week period is counted by § 222 Abs. 1 ZPO with §§ 187 Abs. 1, 188 Abs. 2 BGB, and an end on a Saturday, Sunday or general holiday moves to the next working day (§ 222 Abs. 2 ZPO).

Mahnbescheid: the label is the end of the two weeks in which the debtor is asked to pay or to object (§ 692 Abs. 1 Nr. 3 ZPO). A Widerspruch still counts while no Vollstreckungsbescheid has been issued (§ 694 Abs. 1 ZPO); that reading gives no fixed date, so no other date is listed.

Dismissal: the action against a written dismissal is due three weeks after its receipt (§ 4 S. 1 KSchG, § 7 KSchG; §§ 187 Abs. 1, 188 Abs. 2 BGB). These letters are made so that the three weeks end on a working day in every Land, so no question of moving the end arises. The day the employment ends (§ 622 BGB) is stated, not labelled.

Landlord's notice: the lease ends as § 573c Abs. 1 BGB gives for the day of receipt, and the tenant's Widerspruch must reach the landlord two months before that end (§ 574b Abs. 2 S. 1 BGB), counted back from the end with §§ 187, 188 Abs. 2, 3 BGB: a lease ending on a month's last day gives the last day of the month two months earlier (28 February → 31 December). The other reading takes the same day number two months earlier (28 February → 28 December).

Rent increase: the tenant's period to consent ends with the second calendar month after the month of receipt (§ 558b Abs. 2 S. 1 BGB, § 192 BGB); the consent is a declaration due within a period, so an end on a Saturday, Sunday or holiday moves to the next working day (§ 193 BGB). The other reading leaves the end where it falls.

Operating-cost statement: the tenant's objections are due by the end of the twelfth month after receipt (§ 556 Abs. 3 S. 5 BGB), counted by §§ 187 Abs. 1, 188 Abs. 2, 3 BGB to the day with the receipt day's number, moved off a Saturday, Sunday or holiday (§ 193 BGB). The other reading takes the end of the twelfth calendar month after the month of receipt (§ 192 BGB).

A statement of operating costs given after the end of the twelfth month after its billing period (§ 556 Abs. 3 S. 2 BGB) cannot found a Nachforderung unless the landlord is not responsible for the delay (§ 556 Abs. 3 S. 3 BGB). These statements give no reason for the delay, so the payment they ask for is an optional item.

Withdrawal: 14 days (§ 355 Abs. 2 BGB) from conclusion, or for a sale of goods from receipt of the goods (§ 356 Abs. 2 Nr. 1 a BGB), where the letter with the withdrawal information was handed over on that day (§ 356 Abs. 3 S. 1 BGB); sending the withdrawal in time is enough (§ 355 Abs. 1 S. 5 BGB), and an end on a Saturday, Sunday or holiday moves to the next working day (§ 193 BGB).
